subject: Inverted detection history for multi-season model

messages.author: e33e436208ff4e23
messages.subject: Inverted detection history for multi-season model
parts:
Hello,

 

I'm running a multi-season model on a 15 year data set that has complete detection histories for the most recent years but a lot of missing observations from the early years. Since psi1 is estimated and all the subsequent years are derived, I’m wondering, what effect would inverting the detection histories so that psi1 is actually psi15 have? In theory psi1 would then be estimated using a complete detection history, each subsequent psi parameter would be derived, and gamma and epsilon interpretation would just be reversed. Or would this be erroneous because each psi derivation is contingent upon the previous year and we’re altering the direction of that change? Thanks in advance!

 

Phil

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Inverted detection history for multi-season model
parts:
Dear Phil,

I find this an interesting question. I don't think that you would get different estimates of psi by running the analysis in the correct and the reversed order of time.

Perhaps you can try out and look at the estimates and their SEs ?

Regards  --  Marc

messages.author: 254e2a86eb3ba6a4
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Inverted detection history for multi-season model
parts:
I don't have a complete answer (yet) but I two observations:

(1) I agree that extreme values of psi1 are worth looking into (when you run it forward), but such an extreme value is also what you would get if psi1 is close to 1.0.  Is psi1 approximately equal to 1.0 a possibility with your data?

(2) The pdf that I attached earlier assumed that each transition period would have a separate epsilon and gamma.  But your model makes the restriction that all the epsilon's are equal across time and all of the gamma's are equal across seasons.  While one can construct the reverse Markov chain model that gives equivalent history probabilities (which also give equivalent psi's), the epsilon's and gamma's needed to do that must vary over seasons.  (I can at least prove that for 3 seasons and then would assume that holds for more than 3 seasons.)  So fitting in the reverse direction with that same restriction won't result in the same Markov chain model.

Jim

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Inverted detection history for multi-season model
parts:
Not much more to report other than to give an example (in attached file) that when gamma and epsilon are held constant, then the analysis of the reverse time order fits a different model.  When gamma and epsilon are allowed to vary by season/year, then the forward and reverse time order results in the same model being fitted.  I used the data generation technique in the vignette "Dynamic occupancy models in unmarked" by Marc Kery and Richard Chandler (29-March-2012) to provide simulated data for the attached example.
 
Jim
